newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip at start, profit-taking feared.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip at start, profit-taking feared.

text.p: Danish share prices slipped in early trade on Tuesday, with dealers foreseeing an end to the recent days' record closing highs due to possible profit-taking and EMU doubts.
"There is a strong possibility that investors will indulge in profit-taking today on top of the latest record closing highs. EMU jitters are bound to rub off on us," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index had lost 0.32 point to 170.08 at 0830 GMT after closing 2.26 point higher on Monday at a record closing high for the second consecutive day. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969652
